title: Receive owner files through a Telegram bot
goal: Let one authorized owner send a file to a host-specific Telegram bot, save it as an inert local file, and receive a verified path reply.

evidence.scope: Telegram Bot API documents polling, files and replies. A separately installed private receiver was verified on one host; the public foundation does not ship or activate that receiver.

prerequisites: The owner has a host-specific bot and knows which private chat is authorized.
The selected bot has one update consumer: no competing poller and no active webhook when polling is chosen.
A separately reviewed provider can store files privately, send replies, keep durable receipts and recover after restart.
The canonical bot token and owner binding belong in the external user overlay; a provider may need a protected runtime projection with a verified rotation path.

flows.when: The owner wants to upload files to one host through that host's bot.

steps.action: Verify the selected bot and owner-private recipient against the saved host binding without displaying the token; inspect webhook and existing consumer state.
steps.proof: The bot and owner match the requested host, webhook is empty for polling, and one consumer will own updates.

steps.action: Use the protected overlay token and owner binding to configure a standalone receiver, private file store, size limits, durable offsets and idempotent reply receipts.
steps.proof: Effective configuration and filesystem permissions match the reviewed provider contract; no token appears in public source or logs.

steps.action: Start the single receiver and enable supervised restart and boot activation for the exact host service.
steps.proof: The service is active and enabled, health shows a fresh successful poll, and no second consumer is present.

steps.action: Send one harmless test document to the selected host bot.
steps.proof: The provider records a saved file with restricted access and a sent path-reply receipt; the owner sees the matching reply.

recovery: If the receiver is stopped, distinguish intentional disablement from a crash before enabling it; preserve durable offsets and files.
If webhook, competing polling, token mismatch or uncertain reply delivery is found, stop the cutover and reconcile the exact bot state without dropping updates or blindly resending.
A plain text message is not a file; text-to-Codex routing is a separate provider capability that requires an exact session binding.
On token rotation, update the overlay source and every protected provider projection together, then verify bot identity, fresh polling and an owner-private receipt.
To revoke access, stop the receiver, revoke the bot credential and handle retained private files under the owner's retention policy.

review_triggers: Telegram Bot API polling or file limit change
host bot or owner identity change
failed health, file-save or reply receipt
